source_refs.note: Steps to calculate the Median: a main subheading of 22.2.2 Median, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 191-192.

items: Step 1: Arrange the dataset in ascending or descending order.
Step 2: Count the total number of values in the dataset.
Step 3: If the number of values in the dataset is odd, the median is the value at the position ((n + 1)/2)ᵗʰ.
Step 4: If the number of values in the dataset is even, the median is the average of values at the positions (n/2)ᵗʰ and ((n + 1)/2)ᵗʰ.

blocks.text: For an even number of values the two middle values are at the positions (n/2)ᵗʰ and (n/2 + 1)ᵗʰ, not ((n + 1)/2)ᵗʰ. For n = 6 they are the 3rd and 4th values, as the book's own example uses ((6 + 2)/2 = 4).
blocks.title: Book correction
Example 1 (odd number of values)
blocks.problem: A biologist studied the average height (cm) of five plants in a garden. The heights of the plants are 50cm, 65cm, 60cm, 75cm, and 80cm.
steps: Step 3: n = 5 is odd, the median is the value at the position ((5 + 1)/2) = (6/2) = 3.

blocks.title: Example 1 (even number of values)
blocks.problem: A biologist studied the average weight (kg) of six different animals in a zoo. The weights of the animals are 300kg, 400kg, 330kg, 315kg, 450kg and 500kg.
steps: Step 3: n = 6 is even, the median is the average of value at the position (6/2) = 3 and ((6 + 2)/2) = (8/2) = 4.

blocks.text: The two middle values must be added before dividing: Median = (330 + 400)/2 = 365 kg. Without the brackets, 330 + 400/2 would give 530.
blocks.title: Book correction
